reason: Since the installed release (39b2dd1) the schema gained the table cq_drive_periods with its index, and the model gained the drive identity (DriveId) on DriverRecord, DriverStatus and DriverSummary, the types DrivePeriod, DrivePeriodState and DriveEntry, the requests DriverRequest.Periods and DriverRequest.Drives with their replies, and BackupTable.DrivePeriods; earlier in the same span the model gained what tells a governing session that a person settled what it waits on (AwaitedEnd, the branches Watching, Settled and Released of SessionUnitEvent, the field settled of WaitOutcome.Ended) and the optional field check of PhaseSpan with the per-check usage report, which change no stored row. dev/local-update.sql creates the table and the index as server/src/main/resources/db/001-ledgers.sql declares them, gives every stored driver a new drive identity in its body and its summary, records the state each driver is in as the first period of its drive (the time it stopped, or the time it was last touched), and records that schema's hash; the updater verifies that no other table and no other value of a driver changed, that each driver has exactly one such period, and that the updated database has the structure the new schema declares. The SQL changes nothing when it is applied again. Project archives are not converted; an archive of the installed release is refused by its schema hash. The generated Pi extension changed earlier in this span, so a project that uses Pi runs cq configure pi --replace after the update.
